rationale: Meilisearch is a production-grade, open-source full-text search engine written in Rust. It directly implements the 'fulltext-search' pipeline concern as its core capability, with 706 Rust source files across 381 directories. The milli crate provides the core search engine (indexing + search) with typo tolerance via Levenshtein automata (fuzzy-matching). The index-scheduler crate implements a sophisticated task queue and job scheduling system (queue concern) with autobatching, prioritization, and persistent task storage. The codebase features hybrid search (keyword + vector/semantic), multi-language tokenization (CJK, Hebrew, etc.), faceted filtering, geosearch, document relations, and personalization. Extensive test infrastructure includes unit tests, integration tests, declarative upgrade tests (workloads/tests/*.json), benchmarks with a dedicated dashboard, and fuzzing. CI runs on Linux/Windows/macOS with multiple feature combinations. Licensing is MIT for community edition, BUSL-1.1 for enterprise features.
limitations: Dual licensing (MIT + BUSL-1.1) may restrict enterprise feature use in production without commercial agreement
Not a scraping pipeline component itself - would need integration as a downstream search index
Vector search requires external embedding models (Hugging Face, OpenAI, Ollama) - not self-contained
Rust-based; integration from Python/JS scrapers requires HTTP client or SDK
No built-in browser automation, script generation, self-healing selectors, stealth, or JSON-LD extraction
